title: C-101CC Aviojet (DCS)

sources.title: DCS C-101 Flight Manual (EN), annex C-101CC and smoke system

intro: The C-101CC is the armed version of the Aviojet trainer. It has the same airframe and many of the same panels as the EB, so this guide only lists what is different: the SCAR weapons control box, the optical gun sight, the angle-of-attack display, the V/UHF radio, the gyro platform, the VHF COMM/NAV panel, the ADF radio compass, the radio altimeter and a different flight director panel. Everything else comes from the C-101EB guide.

areas.name: Main instrument panel
areas.text: The big panel in front of the pilot with the flight dials, the engine gauges, the warning lights, the flight director and the UHF radio.

panels.name: Flight instruments (main panel)
panels.text: These are the round dials in the middle of the panel that tell the pilot how fast the plane flies, how high it is, which way it points and whether it is level.
panels.context: The pilot scans these dials all the time during flight. The rear cockpit has its own copy of the same dials, so the instructor sees the same picture.

controls.name: HSI (horizontal situation indicator)
controls.text: The HSI is a compass dial with a moving arrow. It shows which way the plane points, which course the pilot wants to fly and whether the plane is left or right of that course.
controls.context: The pilot sets the wanted course and heading with the two knobs of the forward lower panel. The HSI also shows the distance to a radio beacon and the direction to the station.

controls.name: ADI (attitude director indicator)
controls.text: The ADI is a ball that shows whether the nose is up or down and whether the wings are level, like a small artificial horizon. Two moving bars on it show the pilot how to steer.
controls.context: The pilot uses it most in clouds or at night, when there is no horizon to look at. The steering bars are driven by the flight director buttons.

controls.name: Altitude-encoding altimeter
controls.text: The altimeter shows how high the plane is. A pointer shows the last hundreds of feet and a three-digit counter shows the rest.
controls.context: The front altimeter also passes the height to the radio transponder (IFF), so air traffic radar can read it.

controls.name: VSI (vertical speed indicator)
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the plane climbs or sinks, in feet per minute. The needle sits in the middle when the plane flies level.
controls.context: The manual says it reads up to 6000 feet per minute up or down. The pilot watches it to keep a steady climb or descent.

controls.name: Turn and slip indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the plane turns around its upright axis. A small ball under it shows whether the turn is clean or the plane is sliding sideways.
controls.context: A centred ball means a coordinated turn. It works with its own gyroscope, so it still works when other instruments fail.

controls.name: Clock
controls.text: The clock shows the time of day and also has a stopwatch with a minute hand and a second hand.
controls.context: Pilots use the stopwatch to time legs of a flight, for example between two radio beacons.

controls.name: RMI (radio magnetic indicator)
controls.text: The RMI is a compass dial with two pointers. One pointer shows the direction to a VOR radio beacon, the other shows the direction to a TACAN radio beacon.
controls.context: The compass card turns with the plane, so the pointers show at once where to turn to reach the station.

controls.name: Airspeed and Mach indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the plane flies through the air, in knots. A second scale shows the Mach number, the speed compared with the speed of sound.
controls.context: A small triangle on the rim can be set as a speed reminder, for example the speed for the approach.

controls.name: Vertical accelerometer (G meter)
controls.text: This dial shows how hard the pilot is pushed into the seat. It has one pointer for now and two pointers that remember the highest and lowest values reached.
controls.context: It tells the pilot how close the plane came to its load limit during hard turns.

controls.name: Standby artificial horizon
controls.text: This small ball instrument is a spare horizon. It shows nose up or down and wings level, even if the ADI fails.
controls.context: It has its own gyroscope and power supply from the essential electrical bus. A warning flag shows when it has no power.

controls.name: Trim position indicator
controls.text: This small display shows how far the aileron trim and the elevator trim are set. Trim is a small steady push on the controls so the pilot does not have to hold the stick.
controls.context: The pilot checks that it shows neutral before take-off.

panels.name: Engine and system gauges (main panel)
panels.text: These dials show how the engine and the plane's systems are doing: engine speed, temperature, oil, fuel use, electricity, hydraulic pressure and the flap and speed brake positions.
panels.context: The pilot glances at them after engine start and regularly in flight. A reading outside the normal range is the first sign of a problem.

controls.name: N1 tachometer (fan speed)
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the front part of the engine, the fan, turns. The scale is in percent of the normal maximum speed.
controls.context: The jet has two shafts that turn at different speeds. N1 is the slower, front one.

controls.name: ITT indicator (engine temperature)
controls.text: This dial shows the temperature between the two engine turbines, in degrees Celsius.
controls.context: The pilot watches it during engine start and when giving full power. Too high a temperature can damage the engine.

controls.name: N2 tachometer (core speed)
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the second, inner engine shaft turns, in percent of its normal maximum.
controls.context: During start the starter turns this shaft first. The manual says the starter switches off by itself at 50 percent N2.

controls.name: Oil pressure indicator
controls.text: This dial shows the pressure of the engine oil, in psi. The oil keeps the moving parts of the engine smooth.
controls.context: A red OIL PRESS light on the warning panel comes on when the pressure falls below 25 psi.

controls.name: Oil temperature indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how hot the engine oil is, in degrees Celsius.
controls.context: It is read together with the oil pressure. Hot oil is a sign that the engine or its cooling is in trouble.

controls.name: Fuel flow and fuel used indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how much fuel the engine burns per hour and adds up the fuel used since the last reset.
controls.context: The fuel flow is shown in pounds per hour. The pilot compares fuel used with fuel left to plan the flight.

controls.name: DC bus voltage indicator
controls.text: This voltmeter shows the voltage of the plane's direct-current electricity. It shows the generator voltage when the generator runs and the battery voltage when it does not.
controls.context: The manual says that with the bus tie switch off, the pilot can check each battery by switching the other off.

controls.name: Hydraulic pressure indicator
controls.text: This dial shows the pressure of the hydraulic oil that works the landing gear, flaps, speed brake, brakes and ailerons.
controls.context: A red HYD PRESS light on the warning panel comes on if the pressure falls below 2000 psi. The rear dial repeats the front dial.

panels.name: Red panel light knobs
panels.text: These knobs set how bright the red lights are that light up parts of the panels at night. Red light keeps the pilot's eyes used to the dark.
panels.context: They are used for night flying. The manual lists three of them on the main panel and the game has five in total.

controls.name: ADJUST RED LIGHT knobs (left centre panel, left console)
controls.text: These two knobs set the brightness of the red light for the left centre panel and the left console. Turning a knob makes its light brighter or darker.
controls.context: The manual lists red panel light adjust knobs on the main panel but does not say which is which.

panels.name: Control transfer buttons and gyro controls (main panel)
panels.text: These buttons hand a radio or the navigation set over to this cockpit. The gyro controls keep the compass and horizon instruments correct.
panels.context: Two pilots share one set of radios. Pressing a transfer button in one cockpit takes control of that equipment for this cockpit.

controls.name: V/UHF antenna selector

positions.name: UP
positions.text: The antenna on top of the fuselage is used.

positions.name: AUT
positions.text: The radio chooses the antenna with the best reception by itself.

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The antenna under the fuselage is used.

controls.text: This switch chooses which of the two radio antennas of the V/UHF radio is used: the one on top, the one on the bottom, or automatic.
controls.context: The game names the switch 'V/UHF Antennas Selector' in the C-101CC. In automatic the radio picks the antenna with the better signal.

panels.name: SCAR control unit (stores selection and release)
panels.text: The SCAR unit is the weapons control box of the C-101CC. With its switches the pilot chooses the weapons, picks the pylons (the wing racks that carry them) and arms them.
panels.context: The manual says it holds all the tactical controls of the armament system. The weapons only work when the plane is in the air, because a switch on the right wheel leg cuts the power when the weight is on the wheels.

controls.name: SCAR main control unit (whole box)
controls.text: This is the whole SCAR control box on the instrument panel. Its switches, buttons and selectors are explained one by one below.
controls.context: The SCAR name stands for selection and control and release. The rear cockpit has a repeat of the unit's lights but not of the switches.

controls.name: MASTER ARM switch (weapons master, MAST SW)

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The armament system is without power, except for the emergency jettison.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: Power is available to the armament system.

controls.text: This is the main safety switch for the weapons. With it off nothing can be fired or released, except the emergency jettison.
controls.context: The manual calls it the weapons master switch. The pilot turns it on only when ready to use the weapons.

controls.name: MASTER MODE switch (fixed weapons, CANN-M/G) with cover

positions.name: A/A
positions.text: The gun is armed and the sight is in the air-to-air gun mode.

positions.name: A/G
positions.text: The gun is armed and the sight is in the air-to-ground gun mode.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The gun circuits are off.

controls.text: This switch prepares the guns of the fixed weapons pack, a cannon or machine guns under the cockpits. A guard (cover) protects it from being moved by accident.
controls.context: The manual calls it the fixed weapons switch. With the weapons master switch on and A/A chosen, the gun circuits are powered and the sight is set for air-to-air shooting. A/G sets it for shooting at the ground.

controls.name: PYLON SELECT buttons 1 to 6
controls.text: These six buttons choose which wing racks (pylons) will drop or fire their load. A chosen button lights amber. A green mark shows that the pylon carries a load, and NS in blue shows that it is empty.
controls.context: The buttons are in the same order as the pylons seen from behind the plane.

controls.name: MODE SELECTOR switch (SAF, BOMB, RIP, NC, BM, ROC, 1-1, BRST)

positions.name: SAF
positions.text: Safe: all bomb and rocket arming circuits are off. Only the emergency jettison works.

positions.name: BOMB
positions.text: Bombs are released from the chosen pylons, in pairs if more than one is chosen.

positions.name: RIP
positions.text: Ripple: the stores are released one after the other with the time delay set on the ripple time selector.

positions.name: NC
positions.text: This position has no function.

positions.name: BM
positions.text: Bomb release when a mixed launcher is fitted.

positions.name: ROC
positions.text: Rocket release when a mixed launcher is fitted.
Single rocket release.

positions.name: BRST
positions.text: Several rockets are released.

controls.text: This eight-position dial chooses what the stores do: stay safe, drop bombs, drop bombs one after the other, or fire rockets one at a time or in bursts.
controls.context: SAF is safe: the arming circuits are dead and only the jettison works.

controls.name: RIPPLE TIME selector (70, 90, 120, 150, 200)

positions.text: 70 milliseconds between bombs.
90 milliseconds between bombs.
120 milliseconds between bombs.
150 milliseconds between bombs.
200 milliseconds between bombs.

controls.text: This dial sets the pause, in thousandths of a second, between two bombs in a ripple release.
controls.context: It matters only when the mode selector is on RIP.

controls.name: BOMB ARMING selector (OFF, NS/TL, NS, TL)

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The arming system is off.

positions.name: NS/TL
positions.text: Nose and tail fuzes are armed.

positions.name: NS
positions.text: Only the nose fuze is armed.

positions.name: TL
positions.text: Only the tail fuze is armed.

controls.text: This dial chooses which fuzes (the triggers inside the bombs) are armed: the nose fuze, the tail fuze or both.
controls.context: NS stands for nose and TL for tail. In OFF the arming system is off.

controls.name: SELECTIVE JETTISON SELECTOR (OFF, IN, CEN, OUT)

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The selective jettison system is off.

positions.name: IN
positions.text: The inboard pylons are chosen.

positions.name: CEN
positions.text: The centre pylons are chosen.

positions.name: OUT
positions.text: The outboard pylons are chosen.

controls.text: This dial picks which pylons will be emptied by the selective jettison button: the inner ones, the centre ones or the outer ones.
controls.context: Jettison means dropping the loads without arming them, to get rid of them in a hurry.

controls.name: SELECTIVE JETTISON button
controls.text: Pressing this button drops the loads of the pylons chosen with the selective jettison selector. The loads fall unarmed.
controls.context: The manual says the system is off if the weapons master switch or the selector is OFF.

controls.name: EMERGENCY JETTISON button (guarded)
controls.text: Pressing this guarded button drops all loads at once, whatever the other switches say. The loads fall unarmed, in pairs.
controls.context: The manual says the release goes outboard, inboard and then centre, at intervals of 300 milliseconds. It works while the plane has electrical power.

controls.name: SCAR LIGHT TEST button
controls.text: Pressing this button lights all the lamps of the SCAR units. The ammunition display then shows 888.
controls.context: The rear cockpit has its own button for the lamps of the rear display unit.

panels.name: SCAR display unit
panels.text: The display unit shows the state of the weapons: which pylons are chosen, whether bombs are armed, how many cannon rounds remain and whether a selection error has occurred.
panels.context: There is a display unit in each cockpit. Both show the same pylon choices.

controls.name: SCAR display unit (whole unit)
controls.text: This is the whole SCAR display. It shows an aircraft picture from behind with a light for each pylon, the ARM and SEL ERR lights and the ammunition counter.
controls.context: SEL ERR flashes red when a chosen pylon does not carry the stores that were selected, or when the choice is not symmetrical.

controls.name: CANCEL / mode selected button (MODE SELECTOR/CANCEL)
controls.text: Pressing this button cancels all weapon modes except the emergency jettison. Pressing it again brings the earlier setting back.
controls.context: The lower half of the button shows R for rockets or B for bombs, depending on the chosen mode.

controls.name: INITIAL CANNON LOAD switch

positions.name: FLIGHT
positions.text: Normal position for flight.

positions.name: TEST
positions.text: The remaining rounds are shown even with the weapons master switch off.

controls.text: This switch tells the counter how many rounds the cannon was loaded with at the start. The numbers 5 to 14 mean rounds times 10. TEST shows the rounds left even with the master switch off.
controls.context: The manual says the switch must be on FLIGHT during flight.

panels.name: Optical sight and sight control unit
panels.text: The optical sight is the aiming device on top of the instrument panel. It shows an aiming mark (a reticle) in the pilot's view. The control unit below it switches the sight on and sets how far down the mark points.
panels.context: The manual calls it the RGS2 gyro sight. The mark moves by itself to allow for the plane's turning and the fall of the shells. The rear cockpit has a repeater sight.

controls.name: Optical sight (sight head)
controls.text: The optical sight is a glass in front of the pilot's eyes that shows an aiming mark. The pilot lines the mark up with the target before firing.
controls.context: It is not a switch. The game does not offer a click for the glass itself.

controls.name: Sight brightness knob (reticle illumination)
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the aiming mark brighter or dimmer.
controls.context: The manual says the brightness control is on the lower left of each sight head.

controls.name: Optical sight control unit (whole unit)
controls.text: The control unit below the sight has a power switch, a mode switch and three depression wheels.
controls.context: It is mounted below the optical sight in the front cockpit.

controls.name: OPTICAL SIGHT ON/OFF switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The sight is on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The sight is off.

controls.text: This switch turns the optical sight on or off.
controls.context: The manual lists it as the power switch of the sight.

controls.name: DEPRESSION AUTO/MAN/TEST switch

positions.name: AUTO
positions.text: The mark is tilted by an automatic or pre-set amount.

positions.name: MAN
positions.text: The pilot sets the tilt with the depression wheels.

positions.name: TEST
positions.text: The sight runs its self-test.

controls.text: This switch chooses how the sight tilts the aiming mark downward. AUTO uses a value set in advance, MAN uses the value the pilot dials in, and TEST runs a self-test.
controls.context: The tilt downward is called the depression. It is measured in milliradians, a small angle unit.

controls.name: DEPRESSION selector wheels (x100, x10, x1)
controls.text: These three thumb wheels set the tilt of the aiming mark in milliradians, one for the hundreds, one for the tens and one for the ones.
controls.context: They matter only in MAN mode. The manual says the displayed limit is 199 milliradians.

panels.name: Camera control panel
panels.text: A small panel for the gun camera, a film camera on the sight that records what the pilot saw while shooting.
panels.context: The manual says the front camera starts when the trigger is fired or when the camera button on the stick is pressed.

controls.name: Video switch (ON, STB, OFF)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The position ON named by the game.

positions.name: STB
positions.text: The position STB named by the game.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The position OFF named by the game.

controls.text: This switch is the video switch of the camera control panel. The game offers ON, STB and OFF. The manual shows two switches on the panel, the video power switch and the video recording switch, and does not explain the positions.
controls.context: The game names the control 'Video ON/STB/OFF'.

panels.name: Angle-of-attack indicator and indexer
panels.text: These two displays show how steeply the wing meets the air, which tells the pilot how close the plane is to losing lift. The round indicator is on the panel and a set of three coloured lamps (the indexer) sits near the sight.
panels.context: The manual says the system has an airstream probe, indicators, indexers and the stall warning pedal vibrator. The indexer shows green for the best speed, red when slow and yellow when fast.

controls.name: Angle-of-attack indicator
controls.text: This dial shows the angle of attack in arbitrary units from 0 to 50. OFF shows in the window when the instrument has no power.
controls.context: A few fixed marks on the dial show the best angles for different flight conditions.

controls.name: AOA indicator reference knob
controls.text: Turning this knob on the lower left of the indicator moves a reference mark around the dial.
controls.context: The manual calls it the AOA reference index set knob.

controls.name: Angle-of-attack indexer
controls.text: Three lamps tell the pilot the speed at a glance. Green in the centre means the best speed. Red at the top means too slow. Yellow at the bottom means too fast.
controls.context: The indexer sits on the left side above the instrument panel. It is a display only.

panels.name: Instruments added or changed in the CC
panels.text: These are the dials and switches of the main panel that the C-101CC has in addition to, or instead of, those of the EB version.
panels.context: The CC annex of the manual says its air data computer and navigation set are new, and that no part common to both versions is described again.

controls.name: Standby airspeed indicator
controls.text: This dial shows the plane's speed in knots from 0 to 480. It is a spare, fed directly by the pitot tube.
controls.context: It works without the air data computer and has a white lamp of its own.

controls.name: Standby altimeter
controls.text: This spare altimeter shows the plane's height with a pointer and a drum counter, up to 50000 feet. It is fed directly by the pressure system.
controls.context: Its setting knob is on the lower right of the instrument.

controls.name: Standby altimeter baro adjust knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the air pressure number of the standby altimeter, in millibars.
controls.context: Without the right pressure number the altimeter reads too high or too low.

controls.name: Tap Glass button (standby altimeter)
controls.text: The game names this button 'Tap Glass'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: It sits with the standby altimeter controls in the game.

controls.name: DME selector switch (HOLD, NORM)

positions.name: HOLD
positions.text: The DME keeps reading the distance to the first station.

positions.name: NORM
positions.text: The DME reads the distance to the station that is tuned.

controls.text: This switch decides how the DME (the distance meter to a radio station) works. In HOLD it keeps showing the distance to one station while the radio is tuned to another. In NORM it follows the tuned station.
controls.context: It lets the pilot read the distance to one station while following the direction of another.

controls.name: Radio altimeter switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The radio altimeter is off.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The radio altimeter is on.

controls.text: This switch turns on the radio altimeter, the instrument that measures the height over the ground by bouncing radio waves off it.
controls.context: The manual says it is in the front cockpit and is powered by the secondary DC bus. The ADI shows the radio height.

controls.name: ELT switch (AUT, TEST)
controls.text: This switch controls the emergency locator transmitter, a radio that sends a distress signal after a crash. In AUT it is armed to start by itself after an impact. In TEST it sends its signal so it can be checked.
controls.context: The manual says TEST can also start the transmitter after a successful forced landing.

controls.name: RADIO ALTITUDE SWITCH TEST (ADI)
controls.text: Pressing this button on the ADI tests the radio altitude display and the decision height lamp.
controls.context: The manual lists a radio altitude test switch, part 6 of the ADI of the CC.

controls.name: Decision height set knob and display dimmer
controls.text: Turning this knob on the ADI sets the decision height, the height at which the DH lamp lights up. It also sets the brightness of the number displays of the ADI and HSI.
controls.context: The manual says the DH lamp lights when the plane is at or below the height set.

controls.name: BEARING SELECT pushbutton (HSI)
controls.text: Pressing this button chooses what the pink bearing pointer of the HSI shows: the direction to an ADF station or to a navigation station.
controls.context: The manual says the pointer points to the selected station.

controls.name: MPR LAMP TEST button
controls.text: Pressing this button tests the lamp of the manual power reserve. The manual power reserve is an emergency extra push from the engine.
controls.context: The manual lists the power values for MPR in its engine table for the CC.

controls.name: Altimeter Test Adjust button
controls.text: The game names this button 'Altimeter Test Adjust'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: It is one of the extra clickable parts of the game's cockpit.

panels.name: Flight director mode selector (C-101CC)
panels.text: These push-buttons choose what the flight director does. The flight director moves two steering bars on the ADI, and the pilot follows the bars by hand.
panels.context: The CC annex of the manual shows the panel and describes only the IAS, VS and go-around modes. The IAS and VS modes are not implemented in the game.

controls.name: Flight director mode selector (all buttons)
controls.text: This is the group of push-buttons that choose the steering mode of the flight director. A button lights up when its mode is on.
controls.context: The buttons are explained one by one below.

controls.name: STANDBY MODE button
controls.text: Pressing this button puts the flight director in standby. The steering bars go out of sight.
controls.context: The game names the button 'STANDBY MODE' and its command 'FD STBY mode'. The CC annex does not describe it.

controls.name: HEADING MODE button
controls.text: This button makes the flight director steer toward the heading set on the HSI.
controls.context: The EB manual describes a heading mode that holds the heading set with the heading knob.

controls.name: NAV MODE button
controls.text: The game names this button 'NAV MODE' and its command 'FD NAV MODE mode'. The manual's CC annex shows it on the panel and does not describe it.
controls.context: It belongs to the radio navigation modes of the flight director.

controls.name: APPROACH MODE button
controls.text: The game names this button 'APPROACH MODE' and its command 'FD APP mode'. The manual's CC annex does not describe it.
controls.context: It belongs to the landing approach modes of the flight director.

controls.name: BACK COURSE MODE button
controls.text: The game names this button 'BACK COURSE MODE' and its command 'FD BC mode'. The manual's CC annex does not describe it.
controls.context: A back course approach means flying the runway line from the other side.

controls.name: VOR APPROACH MODE button
controls.text: The game names this button 'VOR APPROACH MODE' and its command 'FD VOR APP mode'. The manual's CC annex does not describe it.
controls.context: A VOR is a ground radio beacon. A VOR approach uses it to guide the plane toward the runway.

controls.name: ALTITUDE MODE button
controls.text: This button makes the flight director show the pitch needed to hold the height at which it was pressed.
controls.context: The EB manual describes this altitude hold mode. The CC annex lists it on the panel.

controls.name: VERTICAL SPEED MODE button
controls.text: This button should make the flight director hold the climb or descent rate. The manual says this mode is not implemented in DCS C-101.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot can hold the TCS button to change the held rate without leaving the mode.

controls.name: INDICATED AIR SPEED MODE button
controls.text: This button should make the flight director hold the airspeed. The manual says this mode is not implemented in DCS C-101.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot can hold the TCS button to change the held speed without leaving the mode.

controls.name: FD panel brightness switch (ON, OFF)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The panel lamps are on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The panel lamps are off.

controls.text: This switch sets the brightness of the flight director panel.
controls.context: The game names it 'FD Panel Brightness' with the commands ON and OFF.

panels.name: V/UHF radio V/TVU-740 control panel
panels.text: This is the control box of the V/UHF radio, the radio for talking to other aircraft and the tower. It can talk on very-high and ultra-high frequencies.
panels.context: The manual says the radio covers 118.000 to 149.975 MHz and 225 to 399.975 MHz and takes its power from the essential DC bus.

controls.name: V/UHF control panel (whole box)
controls.text: This is the whole V/UHF radio control box on the instrument panel. Its switches and knobs are explained below.
controls.context: The manual shows nine parts: frequency selectors, test selector, indicator light, squelch, power transmit selector, channel indicator, channel selector, mode selector and function selector.

controls.name: Function dial (A3, A3+G, DF, OFF)

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The radio is off.

positions.name: A3
positions.text: The position A3 named by the game.

positions.name: A3+G
positions.text: The position A3+G named by the game.

positions.name: DF
positions.text: The position DF named by the game.

controls.text: This dial switches the radio off and chooses how it works. The game offers OFF, A3, A3+G and DF. The manual does not explain the positions.
controls.context: The game names the control 'Function Dial'.

controls.name: Frequency mode dial (G, M, P)

positions.name: G
positions.text: The position G named by the game.

positions.name: M
positions.text: The position M named by the game.

positions.name: P
positions.text: The position P named by the game.

controls.text: This dial chooses how the radio is tuned. The game offers the positions G, M and P. The manual does not explain them.
controls.context: The game names the control 'Frequency Mode Dial'.

controls.name: Frequency selectors (100, 10, 1, 0.1 and 0.025 MHz)
controls.text: These five knobs set the frequency digit by digit, from hundreds of MHz down to steps of 25 kHz.
controls.context: The frequency is the 'station number' of the radio. Both people must tune the same number to hear each other.

controls.name: Preset channel selector
controls.text: This knob chooses a stored channel. The chosen number shows in the channel indicator.
controls.context: A stored channel is like a station button on a car radio.

controls.name: TEST SELECTOR SWITCH
controls.text: The game names this control 'TEST SELECTOR SWITCH'. It is the test selector of the radio. The manual does not describe it further.
controls.context: The manual lists a test selector switch as part 2 of the V/UHF panel.

controls.name: POWER TRANSMIT SELECTOR
controls.text: The game names this switch 'POWER TRANSMIT SELECTOR'. The manual lists it and does not describe it.
controls.context: It belongs to the transmitter part of the radio.

controls.name: Squelch switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The hiss is cut off when no signal is received.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: Noise from the receiver is heard.

controls.text: Squelch cuts the hiss of a radio when nobody talks. This switch turns the squelch of the V/UHF radio on or off.
controls.context: The manual lists a squelch part on the V/UHF panel.

areas.name: Left console
areas.text: The panel to the pilot's left with the engine start switches, the fuel panel, the power lever, the flap lever, the emergency controls and the circuit breakers.

panels.name: Engine control panel (start switches)
panels.text: This panel on the left console starts the jet engine. It has the start and ignition switches, a switch for outside power, a computer button and an anti-ice button.
panels.context: The manual says every cockpit has such a panel, but the engine can be started only from the front cockpit. After the start the engine runs by itself.

controls.name: Engine control switches, anti-ice and GPU (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole group of engine start switches on the left console. Its parts are explained one by one below.
controls.context: The manual says the starter switches itself off at 50 percent N2 (core speed), when the engine can run by itself.

panels.name: Fuel control panel
panels.text: This panel on the left console controls how fuel moves from the wing tanks to the main tank and shows how much fuel is left.
panels.context: The plane has four tanks: one in the fuselage, one in the centre wing and one in each outer wing. The engine always draws from the fuselage tank. The wing tanks feed it through pumps.

controls.name: Fuel panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole fuel panel of the left console. Its pump switches, valve switch and quantity controls are explained one by one below.
controls.context: The manual says the fuel quantity is measured only in the fuselage and centre tanks, and not in the outer wing tanks.

panels.name: Power lever quadrant, flap lever and gear warning silence
panels.text: The power lever, the flap lever and a silence button are mounted together on the left console. The power lever works the engine, the flap lever the flaps.
panels.context: The manual says the front power lever has a friction lock. Both cockpits have a lever, joined by a flexible link.

controls.name: Landing gear warning silence button
controls.text: Pressing this button silences the warning tone that sounds when the wheels are up and the engine power is low.
controls.context: The manual says the tone sounds when a wheel is not down and locked below 6500 feet and 75 percent N1. The amber GEAR light stays on as long as this is true.

controls.name: Flap lever (FLAP POSITION SELECTOR)

positions.name: UP
positions.text: The flaps are fully retracted.

positions.name: TAKEOFF
positions.text: The flaps are set to 10 degrees.

positions.name: DOWN
positions.text: The flaps are set to 30 degrees.

controls.text: This lever sets the flaps, the parts of the wing that slide out to give more lift at low speed. It has three marked positions: UP, TAKEOFF (10 degrees) and DOWN (30 degrees).
controls.context: The pilot sets TAKEOFF for take-off and DOWN for landing. The three windows on the instrument panel show where the flaps are.

panels.name: Emergency panel (left console)
panels.text: This panel holds backup controls for failures of the trim, the speed brake and the ailerons, plus the emergency landing gear handle and the seat height switch.
panels.context: These controls are normally left alone. Several have guards or covers so they cannot be moved by accident.

controls.name: Emergency flight control panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the emergency panel with its trim switch, speed brake button, aileron cutout and test light. Each part is explained below.
controls.context: The manual shows seven parts in its picture: emergency elevator trim switch, servo-actuator cutout switch, emergency speed brake switch, seat elevation switch, press-to-test light, trim tone breaker and thermal breaker.

controls.name: EMERGENCY LANDING GEAR EXTENSION handle
controls.text: Pulling this handle lowers the wheels with a bottle of nitrogen gas if the normal system fails. It works whatever position the gear handle is in.
controls.context: The manual says it can be used only once. After the gear has been lowered this way, it cannot be raised by hydraulics again. The label is EMERG. TREN.

panels.name: Emergency fuel system and rudder trim
panels.text: These controls on the left console belong to a back-up fuel system and to the rudder trim. The back-up fuel system lets the engine keep running if the normal engine computer fails.
panels.context: The manual says the emergency fuel system is not implemented in DCS C-101CC. The rudder trim works and is described in the manual.

controls.name: EMERGENCY FUEL switch with cover
controls.text: This guarded lamp-button switches the emergency fuel system on. ON lights amber. A cover protects it. The manual says the system is for emergencies only and the mission must be aborted.
controls.context: The manual says that this system is not implemented in DCS C-101CC.

controls.name: EMERGENCY FUEL lever
controls.text: This lever sets the fuel flow by hand in the emergency fuel system. Its scale shows pounds of fuel per hour. A lock holds it in place.
controls.context: The manual says that to go back to normal operation the lever must be put to 125 pounds per hour. In the game the system is not implemented.

controls.name: Rudder trim switch

positions.name: LEFT
positions.text: Rudder trim to the left, while held.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: No trim movement.

positions.name: RIGHT
positions.text: Rudder trim to the right, while held.

controls.text: Holding this switch to LEFT or RIGHT moves the rudder trim tab and gives a steady push to the left or right on the rudder. It springs back to the middle.
controls.context: The manual says the maximum trim is 15 degrees. The rear cockpit switch overrides the front one.

panels.name: Circuit breaker panel, part 1 (front left console)
panels.text: These circuit breakers are small push-in safety switches. Each one protects one electrical circuit and pops out when too much current flows.
panels.context: The manual says most electrical circuits are protected by pop-out thermal breakers. The main panel is on the front left console and a secondary panel on the rear left console covers circuits of the rear cockpit only.

areas.name: Right console
areas.text: The panel to the pilot's right with the lights, the audio panel, the radios, the air conditioning and the oxygen controls.

panels.name: Illumination panel (cockpit and outside lights)
panels.text: This panel on the right console switches the lights: the cockpit lights for night flying and the lights on the outside of the plane.
panels.context: The manual says the cockpit lights are controlled in each cockpit, while the outside lights are controlled from the front cockpit only. The rear cockpit has its own lamps for the cabin.

controls.name: Illumination panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole light panel on the right console. Its knobs and switches are explained one by one below.
controls.context: The manual lists seven controls: console lights, integral instrument light, anti-collision light, formation lights, position lights, auxiliary lights and storm lights.

panels.name: Oxygen panel and valve lever
panels.text: This part of the right console holds the controls and gauges for the pilot's breathing oxygen.
panels.context: At high altitude the air is too thin to breathe, so the pilot breathes oxygen from two bottles in the nose of the plane.

controls.name: Oxygen system pressure gauge
controls.text: This gauge shows how much pressure is left in the oxygen bottles.
controls.context: The pressure shows on the front gauge and is repeated on the rear one. A red OXY PRESS light comes on when pressure to the regulator drops below 45 psi.

controls.name: Cabin altimeter
controls.text: This gauge shows the altitude that the air pressure inside the cockpit corresponds to. It works like a normal altimeter.
controls.context: In a pressurized cabin this is lower than the real altitude. The manual says the red CKPT PRESS light comes on at 25000 feet.

controls.name: OXYGEN SUPPLY valve lever

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The oxygen valve is open.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The oxygen valve is closed.

controls.text: This lever opens or closes the oxygen valve of this cockpit.
controls.context: The lever is marked A (open) and C (close). The pilot opens it before flight.

panels.name: Audio control panel (INT)
panels.text: This panel is the volume and radio mixer for the pilot's headset. It switches on the radios the pilot wants to hear and sets how loud each one is. It also controls the intercom between the two crew members.
panels.context: The manual calls it the audio control system AN/AIC-18. It lets each pilot listen to any navigation station and to any radio on his own.

controls.name: Audio panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole audio panel on the right console. Its buttons and knobs are explained one by one below.
controls.context: The panel has one button for each radio and navigation receiver, a selector switch, a general volume knob and a call button.

controls.name: Receiver on/volume buttons (VHF, VOR, MK)
controls.text: Each of these three buttons switches one receiver into the headset and sets its volume. Pulling the button out turns the receiver on. Turning it sets the volume.
controls.context: VHF is the communication radio, VOR is the VOR receiver and MK is the marker beacon receiver. Pulling out the VOR button lets the pilot hear the station's identification tone.

controls.name: MAIN MODE SELECTOR
controls.text: This switch chooses which system the pilot talks to when pressing the push-to-talk switch. The game names it 'MAIN MODE SELECTOR'.
controls.context: The EB manual says the selector must be at INT for talking on the interphone. The CC annex does not describe it separately.

controls.name: Receiver on/volume buttons (V/UHF, DME, ADF)
controls.text: Each of these three buttons switches one more receiver into the headset and sets its volume: the V/UHF radio, the DME distance receiver and the ADF radio compass. Pulling the button out turns the receiver on. Turning it sets the volume.
controls.context: These replace the UHF and TCN buttons of the EB audio panel. The CC annex of the manual shows the audio control panel but does not describe the buttons.

panels.name: HSI remote control panel (front cockpit)
panels.text: These two knobs set the course arrow and the heading marker on the HSI compass dial.
panels.context: The manual says the HSI remote control panel is on the right console of the front cockpit and on the forward lower panel of the rear cockpit.

controls.name: Course knob (HSI remote control)
controls.text: Turning this knob moves the course arrow around the HSI dial. This chooses the radio line the pilot wants to follow.
controls.context: The game offers the commands course knob increase and decrease.

controls.name: Heading knob (HSI remote control)
controls.text: Turning this knob moves the heading marker around the HSI dial. This chooses the direction the pilot wants to fly.
controls.context: The flight director's heading mode steers toward this marker. The game offers heading knob increase and decrease.

panels.name: VHF COMM/NAV control panel (VHF-20B)
panels.text: This panel on the right console controls both the communication radio and the navigation radio. The communication part talks to other aircraft and the tower. The navigation part tunes the VOR and ILS beacons.
panels.context: The manual says the communication part covers 116.000 to 151.975 MHz in steps of 25 kHz and takes its power from the secondary DC bus. Each knob also sets a frequency digit when turned with the mouse wheel.

controls.name: VHF COMM/NAV control panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole VHF communication and navigation panel. Its parts are explained one by one below.
controls.context: The manual shows nine parts: communication switch, three communication selectors and volume, a navigation control switch, two navigation selectors and a test switch.

controls.name: COMM OFF/PWR/TEST switch and 1 MHz frequency knob

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The communication radio is off.

positions.name: PWR
positions.text: The communication radio is on.

positions.name: TEST
positions.text: The radio runs its self-test.

controls.text: This switch turns the communication radio off, on or into a test. Turning it with the mouse wheel changes the frequency in steps of 1 MHz.
controls.context: The game hint calls this the 100 MHz frequency control in the front cockpit and the 1 MHz frequency control in the rear cockpit.

controls.name: COMM volume and 25 kHz frequency knob
controls.text: This knob sets the volume of the communication radio. The mouse wheel changes the frequency in small steps.
controls.context: The manual lists a volume control and a 0.025 MHz frequency selector for the communication radio.

controls.name: NAV control switch and 1 MHz frequency knob

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The navigation radio is off.

positions.name: STBY
positions.text: The position STBY named by the game.

positions.name: NAV
positions.text: The position NAV named by the game.

positions.name: DME
positions.text: The position DME named by the game.

positions.name: OVRD
positions.text: The position OVRD named by the game.

controls.text: This switch chooses what the navigation radio does. The mouse wheel changes the navigation frequency in steps of 1 MHz.
controls.context: The game offers the positions OFF, STBY, NAV, DME and OVRD. The manual does not explain them.

controls.name: NAV volume and 50 kHz frequency knob
controls.text: This knob sets the volume of the navigation radio. The mouse wheel changes the navigation frequency in steps of 50 kHz.
controls.context: The manual lists a navigation volume control and a 50 kHz frequency selector.

controls.name: NAV TEST switch
controls.text: This switch runs a test of the navigation radio. The game names it 'NAV TEST SWITCH'.
controls.context: The manual lists a navigation test switch, part 9 of the panel.

panels.name: ADF-60 control panel
panels.text: The ADF is a radio compass. It points to a radio station on the medium-wave band, which pilots use to find their way. This panel tunes the station.
panels.context: The manual says the ADF-60 covers 190 to 1749.5 kHz and uses the secondary DC bus and the 26 volt AC bus. The bearing pointer on the HSI can show the ADF direction.

controls.name: ADF control panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole ADF control panel on the right console. Its parts are explained below.
controls.context: The manual shows seven parts: tone switch, transfer switch, frequency selectors and gain control, and the function selector.

controls.name: ADF TONE switch
controls.text: The game names this switch 'ADF Tone Switch'. It turns the ADF tone on or off.
controls.context: The manual lists a tone switch as part 1 of the panel.

controls.name: ADF TRANSFER switch
controls.text: This switch is the transfer switch of the ADF. The manual does not describe it further.
controls.context: The manual lists a transfer switch as part 2 of the panel.

controls.name: ADF left frequency selector
controls.text: This control sets the left digits of the ADF frequency. Three knobs sit one over another. The game hint says: mouse wheel for the middle knob, left button and wheel for the lower knob, right button and wheel for the upper knob.
controls.context: The manual lists frequency selectors in steps of 100 kHz, 10 kHz and 0.5 kHz.

controls.name: ADF right frequency selector
controls.text: This control sets the right digits of the ADF frequency in the same way as the left one, with three knobs one over another.
controls.context: The two selectors together set the frequency in the range 190 to 1749.5 kHz.

controls.name: ADF function selector and gain control
controls.text: This knob chooses the working mode of the ADF and sets the gain, which is how strongly the signal is amplified. A left or right click changes the mode and the mouse wheel changes the gain.
controls.context: The manual lists the function selector and the gain control as parts 6 and 7 of the panel.

panels.name: Telebriefing light and canopy fracturing handle
panels.text: The telebriefing light and the canopy fracturing handle sit on the right console. The light shows that a ground telephone line is plugged in. The handle breaks the canopy glass in an emergency.
panels.context: The manual says the telebriefing line is cut when the plane taxis away, and that the telebriefing is not implemented in DCS C-101.

controls.name: TELEBRIEFING indicator light
controls.text: This light on the front right console shows that the telebriefing line is working. Over this line the ground controller can brief the pilot while the plane stands on the apron.
controls.context: The manual says that telebriefing is not implemented in DCS C-101.

controls.name: CANOPY EMERGENCY FRACTURING handle (with safety pin)
controls.text: Pulling this T-shaped handle fires a cord along the canopy edge that shatters the glass. A safety pin keeps the handle from being pulled by accident.
controls.context: The manual says there is one on each right console and that each breaks only the canopy of its own cockpit.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: instrument panel
areas.text: The instrument panel of the rear cockpit. It has the same dials as the front panel, and the radios, so the instructor can see and do the same.

panels.name: Red panel light knobs (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These knobs set how bright the red lights are that light up parts of the panels at night. Red light keeps the pilot's eyes used to the dark.
panels.context: They are used for night flying. The manual lists three of them on the main panel and the game has five in total. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: ADJUST RED LIGHT knobs (left centre panel, left console)
controls.text: These two knobs set the brightness of the red light for the left centre panel and the left console. Turning a knob makes its light brighter or darker.
controls.context: The manual lists red panel light adjust knobs but does not say which is which. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

panels.name: Flight instruments (main panel) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These are the round dials in the middle of the panel that tell the pilot how fast the plane flies, how high it is, which way it points and whether it is level.
panels.context: The pilot scans these dials all the time during flight. The rear cockpit has its own copy of the same dials, so the instructor sees the same picture. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Altimeter baro adjust knob
controls.text: The game names this knob 'Altimeter Baro Adjust (No function)'. In the rear cockpit of the C-101CC it does nothing.
controls.context: The rear altimeter has no setting function in the game. The standby altimeter has its own setting knob.

panels.name: Control transfer buttons and gyro controls (main panel) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These buttons hand a radio or the navigation set over to this cockpit. The gyro controls keep the compass and horizon instruments correct.
panels.context: Two pilots share one set of radios. Pressing a transfer button in one cockpit takes control of that equipment for this cockpit. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Fast erect switch (gyro platform)
controls.text: Pressing this control makes the gyro system stand upright quickly if the horizon picture has gone wrong. In the C-101CC it belongs to the gyro platform.
controls.context: The front cockpit has the gyro platform control panel on the pedestal. The game names the rear control 'Fast Erect'.

panels.name: SCAR control unit (stores selection and release) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: The SCAR unit is the weapons control box of the C-101CC. With its switches the pilot chooses the weapons, picks the pylons (the wing racks that carry them) and arms them.
panels.context: The manual says it holds all the tactical controls of the armament system. The weapons only work when the plane is in the air, because a switch on the right wheel leg cuts the power when the weight is on the wheels. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: EMERGENCY JETTISON button (guarded)
controls.text: Pressing this guarded button drops all loads at once, whatever the other switches say. The loads fall unarmed, in pairs.
controls.context: The manual says the release goes outboard, inboard and then centre, at intervals of 300 milliseconds. It works while the plane has electrical power.

controls.name: SCAR LIGHT TEST button
controls.text: Pressing this button lights all the lamps of the SCAR units. The ammunition display then shows 888.
controls.context: The rear cockpit has its own button for the lamps of the rear display unit.

panels.name: SCAR display unit (rear cockpit)
panels.text: The display unit shows the state of the weapons: which pylons are chosen, whether bombs are armed, how many cannon rounds remain and whether a selection error has occurred.
panels.context: There is a display unit in each cockpit. Both show the same pylon choices. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: CANCEL / mode selected button (MODE SELECTOR/CANCEL)
controls.text: Pressing this button cancels all weapon modes except the emergency jettison. Pressing it again brings the earlier setting back.
controls.context: The lower half of the button shows R for rockets or B for bombs, depending on the chosen mode.

controls.name: INITIAL CANNON LOAD switch

positions.name: FLIGHT
positions.text: Normal position for flight.

positions.name: TEST
positions.text: The remaining rounds are shown even with the weapons master switch off.

controls.text: This switch tells the counter how many rounds the cannon was loaded with at the start. The numbers 5 to 14 mean rounds times 10. TEST shows the rounds left even with the master switch off.
controls.context: The manual says the switch must be on FLIGHT during flight.

panels.name: Optical sight and sight control unit (rear cockpit)
panels.text: The optical sight is the aiming device on top of the instrument panel. It shows an aiming mark (a reticle) in the pilot's view. The control unit below it switches the sight on and sets how far down the mark points.
panels.context: The manual calls it the RGS2 gyro sight. The mark moves by itself to allow for the plane's turning and the fall of the shells. The rear cockpit has a repeater sight. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Sight brightness knob (reticle illumination)
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the aiming mark brighter or dimmer.
controls.context: The manual says the brightness control is on the lower left of each sight head.

panels.name: Angle-of-attack indicator and indexer (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These two displays show how steeply the wing meets the air, which tells the pilot how close the plane is to losing lift. The round indicator is on the panel and a set of three coloured lamps (the indexer) sits near the sight.
panels.context: The manual says the system has an airstream probe, indicators, indexers and the stall warning pedal vibrator. The indexer shows green for the best speed, red when slow and yellow when fast. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: AOA indicator reference knob
controls.text: Turning this knob on the lower left of the indicator moves a reference mark around the dial.
controls.context: The manual calls it the AOA reference index set knob.

panels.name: Instruments added or changed in the CC (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These are the dials and switches of the main panel that the C-101CC has in addition to, or instead of, those of the EB version.
panels.context: The CC annex of the manual says its air data computer and navigation set are new, and that no part common to both versions is described again. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Standby altimeter baro adjust knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the air pressure number of the standby altimeter, in millibars.
controls.context: Without the right pressure number the altimeter reads too high or too low.

controls.name: Tap Glass button (standby altimeter)
controls.text: The game names this button 'Tap Glass'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: It sits with the standby altimeter controls in the game.

controls.name: DME selector switch (HOLD, NORM)

positions.name: HOLD
positions.text: The DME keeps reading the distance to the first station.

positions.name: NORM
positions.text: The DME reads the distance to the station that is tuned.

controls.text: This switch decides how the DME (the distance meter to a radio station) works. In HOLD it keeps showing the distance to one station while the radio is tuned to another. In NORM it follows the tuned station.
controls.context: It lets the pilot read the distance to one station while following the direction of another.

controls.name: RADIO ALTITUDE SWITCH TEST (ADI)
controls.text: Pressing this button on the ADI tests the radio altitude display and the decision height lamp.
controls.context: The manual lists a radio altitude test switch, part 6 of the ADI of the CC.

controls.name: Decision height set knob and display dimmer
controls.text: Turning this knob on the ADI sets the decision height, the height at which the DH lamp lights up. It also sets the brightness of the number displays of the ADI and HSI.
controls.context: The manual says the DH lamp lights when the plane is at or below the height set.

controls.name: BEARING SELECT pushbutton (HSI)
controls.text: Pressing this button chooses what the pink bearing pointer of the HSI shows: the direction to an ADF station or to a navigation station.
controls.context: The manual says the pointer points to the selected station.

controls.name: MPR LAMP TEST button
controls.text: Pressing this button tests the lamp of the manual power reserve. The manual power reserve is an emergency extra push from the engine.
controls.context: The manual lists the power values for MPR in its engine table for the CC.

controls.name: Altimeter Test Adjust button
controls.text: The game names this button 'Altimeter Test Adjust'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: It is one of the extra clickable parts of the game's cockpit.

panels.name: Flight director mode selector (C-101CC) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These push-buttons choose what the flight director does. The flight director moves two steering bars on the ADI, and the pilot follows the bars by hand.
panels.context: The CC annex of the manual shows the panel and describes only the IAS, VS and go-around modes. The IAS and VS modes are not implemented in the game. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: FD panel brightness switch (ON, OFF)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The panel lamps are on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The panel lamps are off.

controls.text: This switch sets the brightness of the flight director panel.
controls.context: The game names it 'FD Panel Brightness' with the commands ON and OFF.

panels.name: V/UHF radio V/TVU-740 control panel (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This is the control box of the V/UHF radio, the radio for talking to other aircraft and the tower. It can talk on very-high and ultra-high frequencies.
panels.context: The manual says the radio covers 118.000 to 149.975 MHz and 225 to 399.975 MHz and takes its power from the essential DC bus. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Function dial (A3, A3+G, DF, OFF)

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The radio is off.

positions.name: A3
positions.text: The position A3 named by the game.

positions.name: A3+G
positions.text: The position A3+G named by the game.

positions.name: DF
positions.text: The position DF named by the game.

controls.text: This dial switches the radio off and chooses how it works. The game offers OFF, A3, A3+G and DF. The manual does not explain the positions.
controls.context: The game names the control 'Function Dial'.

controls.name: Frequency mode dial (G, M, P)

positions.name: G
positions.text: The position G named by the game.

positions.name: M
positions.text: The position M named by the game.

positions.name: P
positions.text: The position P named by the game.

controls.text: This dial chooses how the radio is tuned. The game offers the positions G, M and P. The manual does not explain them.
controls.context: The game names the control 'Frequency Mode Dial'.

controls.name: Frequency selectors (100, 10, 1, 0.1 and 0.025 MHz)
controls.text: These five knobs set the frequency digit by digit, from hundreds of MHz down to steps of 25 kHz.
controls.context: The frequency is the 'station number' of the radio. Both people must tune the same number to hear each other.

controls.name: Preset channel selector
controls.text: This knob chooses a stored channel. The chosen number shows in the channel indicator.
controls.context: A stored channel is like a station button on a car radio.

controls.name: TEST SELECTOR SWITCH
controls.text: The game names this control 'TEST SELECTOR SWITCH'. It is the test selector of the radio. The manual does not describe it further.
controls.context: The manual lists a test selector switch as part 2 of the V/UHF panel.

controls.name: POWER TRANSMIT SELECTOR
controls.text: The game names this switch 'POWER TRANSMIT SELECTOR'. The manual lists it and does not describe it.
controls.context: It belongs to the transmitter part of the radio.

controls.name: Squelch switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The hiss is cut off when no signal is received.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: Noise from the receiver is heard.

controls.text: Squelch cuts the hiss of a radio when nobody talks. This switch turns the squelch of the V/UHF radio on or off.
controls.context: The manual lists a squelch part on the V/UHF panel.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: right console
areas.text: The rear copies of the lights, audio panel, radios, air conditioning and oxygen controls.

panels.name: Audio control panel (INT) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel is the volume and radio mixer for the pilot's headset. It switches on the radios the pilot wants to hear and sets how loud each one is. It also controls the intercom between the two crew members.
panels.context: The manual calls it the audio control system AN/AIC-18. It lets each pilot listen to any navigation station and to any radio on his own. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Receiver on/volume buttons (VHF, VOR, MK)
controls.text: Each of these three buttons switches one receiver into the headset and sets its volume. Pulling the button out turns the receiver on. Turning it sets the volume.
controls.context: VHF is the communication radio, VOR is the VOR receiver and MK is the marker beacon receiver. Pulling out the VOR button lets the pilot hear the station's identification tone. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: MAIN MODE SELECTOR
controls.text: This switch chooses which system the pilot talks to when pressing the push-to-talk switch. The game names it 'MAIN MODE SELECTOR'.
controls.context: The EB manual says the selector must be at INT for talking on the interphone. The CC annex does not describe it separately. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Receiver on/volume buttons (V/UHF, DME, ADF)
controls.text: Each of these three buttons switches one more receiver into the headset and sets its volume: the V/UHF radio, the DME distance receiver and the ADF radio compass. Pulling the button out turns the receiver on. Turning it sets the volume.
controls.context: These replace the UHF and TCN buttons of the EB audio panel. The CC annex of the manual shows the audio control panel but does not describe the buttons. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

panels.name: VHF COMM/NAV control panel (VHF-20B) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel on the right console controls both the communication radio and the navigation radio. The communication part talks to other aircraft and the tower. The navigation part tunes the VOR and ILS beacons.
panels.context: The manual says the communication part covers 116.000 to 151.975 MHz in steps of 25 kHz and takes its power from the secondary DC bus. Each knob also sets a frequency digit when turned with the mouse wheel. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: COMM OFF/PWR/TEST switch and 1 MHz frequency knob

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The communication radio is off.

positions.name: PWR
positions.text: The communication radio is on.

positions.name: TEST
positions.text: The radio runs its self-test.

controls.text: This switch turns the communication radio off, on or into a test. Turning it with the mouse wheel changes the frequency in steps of 1 MHz.
controls.context: The game hint calls this the 100 MHz frequency control in the front cockpit and the 1 MHz frequency control in the rear cockpit.

controls.name: COMM volume and 25 kHz frequency knob
controls.text: This knob sets the volume of the communication radio. The mouse wheel changes the frequency in small steps.
controls.context: The manual lists a volume control and a 0.025 MHz frequency selector for the communication radio.

controls.name: NAV control switch and 1 MHz frequency knob

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The navigation radio is off.

positions.name: STBY
positions.text: The position STBY named by the game.

positions.name: NAV
positions.text: The position NAV named by the game.

positions.name: DME
positions.text: The position DME named by the game.

positions.name: OVRD
positions.text: The position OVRD named by the game.

controls.text: This switch chooses what the navigation radio does. The mouse wheel changes the navigation frequency in steps of 1 MHz.
controls.context: The game offers the positions OFF, STBY, NAV, DME and OVRD. The manual does not explain them.

controls.name: NAV volume and 50 kHz frequency knob
controls.text: This knob sets the volume of the navigation radio. The mouse wheel changes the navigation frequency in steps of 50 kHz.
controls.context: The manual lists a navigation volume control and a 50 kHz frequency selector.

panels.name: Telebriefing light and canopy fracturing handle (rear cockpit)
panels.text: The telebriefing light and the canopy fracturing handle sit on the right console. The light shows that a ground telephone line is plugged in. The handle breaks the canopy glass in an emergency.
panels.context: The manual says the telebriefing line is cut when the plane taxis away, and that the telebriefing is not implemented in DCS C-101. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: CANOPY EMERGENCY FRACTURING handle (with safety pin)
controls.text: Pulling this T-shaped handle fires a cord along the canopy edge that shatters the glass. A safety pin keeps the handle from being pulled by accident.
controls.context: The manual says there is one on each right console and that each breaks only the canopy of its own cockpit.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: forward left and right panels
areas.text: The rear copies of the gear handle panel and the electrical switches.

panels.name: Forward left panel (landing gear and brakes) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel at the lower left of the instrument panel holds the landing gear handle, the parking brake, the landing lights, the pitot heat and the stall warning switches.
panels.context: The pilot uses it on every take-off and landing: gear up after take-off, gear down before landing, lights for taxiing, brake handle when parking. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: STALL WARNING POWER switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The stall warning system is powered.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The stall warning system is switched off.

controls.text: This switch turns the stall warning system on or off. The system warns the pilot, by shaking the rudder pedals, before the wing stops flying.
controls.context: A stall is when the wing flies too slowly and loses its lift. The pedals start to shake about 10 to 15 knots before that point.

controls.name: STALL WARNING TEST button
controls.text: Holding this button on TEST checks the stall warning. The amber STALL light lights up and, after about 8 seconds, the pedals shake. The game also offers a RESET command.
controls.context: The manual describes a second test position, TRANSM, that checks the angle-of-attack sensor circuits.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: left console
areas.text: The rear copies of the engine start switches, the fuel panel, the power lever with the flap lever, the emergency panel and the secondary circuit breaker panel.

panels.name: Circuit breaker panel, part 1 (rear left console)
panels.text: These circuit breakers are small push-in safety switches. Each one protects one electrical circuit and pops out when too much current flows.
panels.context: The manual says most electrical circuits are protected by pop-out thermal breakers. The main panel is on the front left console and a secondary panel on the rear left console covers circuits of the rear cockpit only.

controls.name: STALL WARNING SYSTEM circuit breaker

positions.name: IN
positions.text: The breaker is pushed in and the circuit has power.

positions.name: OUT
positions.text: The breaker is popped out and the circuit has no power.

controls.text: The game names this circuit breaker 'STALL WARNING SYSTEM'. The manual does not describe it.
controls.context: A circuit breaker is a safety switch that pops out when too much current flows. This one is labelled STALL WARNING SYSTEM on the panel.

panels.name: Emergency panel (left console) (rear cockpit)
panels.text: This panel holds backup controls for failures of the trim, the speed brake and the ailerons, plus the emergency landing gear handle and the seat height switch.
panels.context: These controls are normally left alone. Several have guards or covers so they cannot be moved by accident. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Pitch trim breaker (thermal breaker)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The emergency trim circuit has power.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The emergency trim circuit is cut off.

controls.text: This is the thermal breaker that protects the emergency trim. It pops out and cuts the power if the trim motor takes too much current.
controls.context: The manual says this breaker is found only in the front cockpit.

panels.name: Emergency fuel system and rudder trim (rear cockpit)
panels.text: These controls on the left console belong to a back-up fuel system and to the rudder trim. The back-up fuel system lets the engine keep running if the normal engine computer fails.
panels.context: The manual says the emergency fuel system is not implemented in DCS C-101CC. The rudder trim works and is described in the manual. This is the copy in the rear (instructor) cockpit.

controls.name: Rudder trim switch

positions.name: LEFT
positions.text: Rudder trim to the left, while held.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: No trim movement.

positions.name: RIGHT
positions.text: Rudder trim to the right, while held.

controls.text: Holding this switch to LEFT or RIGHT moves the rudder trim tab and gives a steady push to the left or right on the rudder. It springs back to the middle.
controls.context: The manual says the maximum trim is 15 degrees. The rear cockpit switch overrides the front one.

areas.name: Stick and power lever
areas.text: The control stick and the power lever, the two controls the pilot's hands hold most of the time, with the buttons and switches on their grips.

panels.name: Control stick grip
panels.text: The control stick is the lever between the pilot's knees. Tilting it left and right rolls the plane, and moving it forward and back pitches the nose down and up. The buttons on the grip are used without taking a hand off it.
panels.context: Each of the two cockpits has its own stick. The manual lists eight parts on the grip: transmit button, stores release button with guard, safety catch, fixed weapons trigger, camera button, rain repellent, trim cut and trim switch.

controls.name: Fixed weapons trigger (gun)
controls.text: Pulling this trigger fires the gun and the other weapons the pilot has chosen. A safety catch in front of it must be opened first.
controls.context: The CC manual's weapon procedures all end with 'aim and depress trigger'. The trigger also starts the gun camera.

controls.name: Stores release button
controls.text: In the game this guarded button on top of the grip is bound to releasing stores such as bombs and rockets.
controls.context: The CC manual describes releasing stores with the trigger and does not list this button separately. The smoke system is described for the EB only.

panels.name: Power lever grip
panels.text: The power lever is the engine control on the left console. Pushing it forward gives more engine power and pulling it back gives less. It is like the gas pedal of a car. Switches on the grip are used with the thumb.
panels.context: Each cockpit has its own lever, joined together. The manual says each grip has a speed brake switch, a manual fuel enrichment button and a PTT microphone switch.

controls.name: Sight head range selector

positions.name: up
positions.text: Range step: next, wider.

positions.name: middle
positions.text: No change.

positions.name: down
positions.text: Range step: previous, narrower.

controls.text: This thumb switch on the power lever grip changes the width of the aiming mark of the sight, so it can be matched to the apparent size of a target at a given range.
controls.context: The manual says the front power lever grip has a sight head range selector for stadiametric ranging, which means measuring the distance by the target's size.

areas.name: Centre pedestal and forward lower panel
areas.text: The centre stand under the instrument panel.

panels.name: Gyroscope platform control panel (AS-339)
panels.text: This panel controls the gyro system that gives the compass and horizon instruments their picture. It is used to start and correct the gyros.
panels.context: The manual says the system has a gyro unit, an electronic amplifier and this control panel on the pedestal, plus a sensor in the right wing tip that finds magnetic north.

controls.name: Gyro platform control panel (whole panel)
controls.text: This is the whole gyro platform control panel on the pedestal. The manual shows eight parts. Its controls are explained below.
controls.context: The manual says to use the synchronizer knob to correct the heading according to the synchronization indicator.

controls.name: Function selector switch
controls.text: The game names this control 'Function Selector'. It chooses how the gyro system works. The manual does not describe its positions.
controls.context: The manual lists it as part 8 of the gyro platform control panel.

controls.name: Synchronizer and heading set knob
controls.text: Turning this knob corrects the heading of the compass system. The pilot turns it according to the synchronization indicator.
controls.context: The manual says the gyro drifts slowly, so this correction is needed from time to time.

controls.name: Latitude correction knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the latitude correction of the gyro system, which means how far north or south the plane is.
controls.context: The manual lists a latitude correction control, number 3 of the panel.

controls.name: Hemisphere switch (N, S)

positions.name: N
positions.text: Northern hemisphere.

positions.name: S
positions.text: Southern hemisphere.

controls.text: This switch tells the gyro system whether the plane is in the northern or the southern half of the world.
controls.context: It goes together with the latitude correction knob.

controls.name: Magnetic variation control (0, 15E, 15W)

positions.text: No correction.

positions.name: 15E
positions.text: 15 degrees east.

positions.name: 15W
positions.text: 15 degrees west.

controls.text: This switch sets the magnetic variation, the difference between true north and the north of the compass. The game offers 0, 15 degrees east and 15 degrees west.
controls.context: The manual lists a magnetic variation control as part 2 of the panel.

controls.name: Fast erect pushbutton
controls.text: Pressing this button makes the gyros stand upright quickly, if the horizon picture has gone wrong.
controls.context: The manual calls it the fast erect pushbutton, part 1 of the panel.

areas.name: Rear cockpit: pedestal and ejection seat
